description:
We bring:

Web development and software engineering (front/back end, APIs, data pipelines)

We’re looking for:

Agriculture: understand crop rotations, soil health, and real farming decisions

Geology or science: soil conditions, climate, water, and erosion

Programmers: experience in data analysis or working with remote sensing data

Business & pitching: shape the story and help us present the idea to judges

You don’t need to fit neatly into one of these. Feel free to reach out regardless!
summary: Our product is an application titled Loam to provide farmers with recommended crop rotation data, a marketplace for finding land, field information, and future predictions related to climate change. It is important for new farmers as they enter the industry to assist them in rotation planning and provide resources. For current farmers, it assists them with understanding ideal conditions and updates with the current climate and weather, assisting in the prediction of climate change for ideal yielding. Farmers can input their tested soil data and have information delivered to them through Loam.
details:
Loam is a web application developed to assist farmers in crop rotation planning and adaptation to climate change. One of its capabilities is to read soil data inputted from a farmer and use that to calculate properties connected to the field. Loam contains a land marketplace feature which allows farmers to view properties being sold and their characteristics. The information provided for each plot of land includes an overview, the climate, soil and water data, as well as a weather forecast. Additionally, there is a field info section that allows the user to select a plot of land and view a productivity map for growing certain crops as well as elevation and NDVI vegetation data. Finally, there is a crop planner to process information provided and assist with the development of a crop rotation schedule.

The front end of Loam was developed using React, Next.js, and Mapbox. Google Cloud Storage stores the data sets while Rasterio and Shapely extract it. 

When making our project, we considered real factors that affect farmers. We interviewed two farmers in the greater Ottawa area and applied their feedback to our project. One farmer had mentioned having a marketplace to check for land while another mentioned including parameters that could be useful to account for climate change. In conversation with a third farmer, it was mentioned we should add weather data to observe how it affects crops as well as economic impact. We did extensive research on crop rotation and took into account crop-family rules, soil-fit heuristics, and water-demand categories to develop our crop rotation algorithm. Our desired impact is to help real farmers by assessing what the community requires and providing it.

Tools used in the project were:

  • Google Docs: Internal organization of resources used
  • Notion: Project and team organization
  • Canva: Development of presentation
  • GitHub: Group code and web application development
  • Google Cloud Storage: Storage of APIs and datasets used
  • Next.js and React: Interactive interface
  • Mapbox: Field visualization
  • Python FastAPI: Processing of field data requests
  • EarthData: Datasets were collected from it
    • Calculate terrain and soil summaries

Creativity and factors considered:

Our team wanted to ensure farmers’ needs were considered and to develop an application suitable to them. Loam takes information from NASA satellite databases and converts it into a format that is simple and easy to use as supplementary information to support farm effectiveness. It makes farming more accessible for first-generation farmers and ensures to take feedback from our community to provide a meaningful impact. We have considered climate change and the effects of AI data centers and further modern advancements on farming and desire to develop it further. In the future, we plan to incorporate a soil moisture map, NDRE and MSAVI vegetation, and soil brightness.
